correctness.rationale: The proof begins with the exact and publicly verified complete-bipartite facet classification (arXiv:1807.07678v1 Proposition 3.4). Direct projection yields squared normal norm \(s-t^2/N\); antipodal facets show the centered radius is globally optimal among all centers. Pairwise balanced sign vectors span the zero-sum subspace if part size is even and the full coordinate subspace if odd. Tight normals force the stated center affine hull; noncontact inequalities are strict at the origin, giving its full relative dimension. For even q the residual sign constraints reduce to an increasing one-variable ratio, whose first permissible \(t=2\) yields the exact bound. Both equal-part regimes are checked, including duplicate constant facet labels at \(p=q=2\). Exact-rational independent checks cover 49 profiles and 30676 facet labels; only the analytical steps support the infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: The geometric question is intrinsic to a widely studied canonical root-polytope family, not an arbitrary parameter slice. It classifies all centers rather than just computing a radius, compresses exponentially many sign constraints on the larger even part to one scalar interval, and exhibits a sharp uniqueness criterion (equal odd part sizes only) plus a complete nontrivial equal-even segment with endpoint tangent-facet transitions. For unequal parts the incenter space has arbitrarily high dimension p or p-1, unlike the star. The statement is a natural all-parameter classification and provides an explicit route to optimize center selection.
